Restoring the 256 MiB floor drained the job to a ready CMAF tree

sc4_reference_mode.ownership_rule: three layers, in this order. (1) PREFIX SCOPING: the sweep lists only web-videos, thumbnails, storyboards, captions, streaming-playlists, playlist-thumbnails; anything else - videos/, foreign/, avatars/, uploads/, .vidra/ - is never enumerated. (2) MINTED-KEY SHAPE (mediagc.isMintedKey): inside a swept prefix the segment below the prefix, cut at its FIRST dot, must parse as a UUID; if it does not, the object was laid out by another system and is KEPT, and this test runs BEFORE every per-prefix question. (3) BUCKET OWNERSHIP (.vidra/owner holding this install's identity) gates destructive sweeps only - a dry run is always allowed, because reporting what would be deleted from a store that is not ours is how an operator finds out it is not ours
sc4_reference_mode.adoption_interlock: sqlcgen.CountForeignLayoutMediaRefs counts video_files whose storage_key is under web-videos/ but not under web-videos/<its own video_id>, plus streaming_playlists whose master_key is not under streaming-playlists/<its own video_id>/. Non-zero (or unanswerable) refuses AdoptBucket

MinIO stands in for the recorded B2 hazards; it has no equivalent of B2's separate deleteFiles entitlement and no object-lock/versioning was configured, so the 'B2 bucket-GC destruction' and 'B2 versioning double-billing' risks are NOT retired by this run
findings: A bucket write refusal and a bucket-full refusal are both a bare 500 internal_error / 'an unexpected error occurred'. The actionable sentence exists and reaches the server log; the operator sees nothing. Same class as A17/A27's bare echo.NewHTTPError 503s that the 5xx scrubber eats.

There is no write probe on the boot path. storage.ProbeWrite exists and its own doc comment cites a real migration that ran three minutes on a read-only key, but main() only calls EnsureBucket (a HeadBucket) - so an instance boots green on a credential that cannot store a byte.

The api's request logger writes the full storage key into the error line ('storage: s3: put "web-videos/<uuid>.mp4"'). The worker's job logger redacts it ([redacted-key], core#190). This is the api-side half of A35's open 'core still logs object_key/storage_key' finding.

HLS/DASH playlists are rewritten in memory and therefore carry no Accept-Ranges and answer a Range request with 200. Correct, but it means a Range probe over the advertised tree is only meaningful on segments and the original.

docs/evidence/*.sh is linted by nothing in meta CI - the shell lint loop covers bootstrap.sh, install.sh, tests/*.sh and deploy/*.sh only. This planter was linted by hand. A39 closed exactly this gap for tests/.

for_other_items.A32 (INT-09 presign): the api logged 'direct object delivery available backend=s3://... note: enable with the delivery_presign_enabled instance setting', so the presign seam is live and OFF by default. TestS3PresignGetAsPinsResponseHeaders passes against MinIO, so the response-header pinning works on a path-style endpoint; what is untested is a real cross-origin bucket's CORS, which is what A32 needs.
for_other_items.A33 (INT-10 CDN): every media response here carries `cache-control: private, ...` (max-age 3600 on the original, 300 on images, 0 on the HLS tree), so nothing in the api-proxy path is cacheable by a shared edge as shipped. The playlist rewrite adds a ?v=<tag> to every child URI, which is the versioning handle an edge purge would key on.
for_other_items.A34 (OPS-01 multi-host): the 'no host-local media assumption' precondition is met on S3: an api process started in an empty working directory served the entire catalogue and created nothing on local disk. The only local path left is the transcode scratch (TMPDIR), which is per-worker and disposable - so an api/worker split across hosts has no shared-volume requirement in s3 mode.
